name: Connecticut veterans: Office of Advocacy and Assistance for claims help
organization: Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Advocacy and Assistance
description: Accredited Veteran Service Officers in five district offices (Rocky Hill, Norwich, Milford, Fairfield and Waterbury) help veterans and families with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and state benefits at no charge. Each town also names a Municipal Veterans Representative who can point you to help.
next_step: Choose a county above for its district office, or call the Office of Advocacy and Assistance at 860-616-3685.
constraints: Districts follow congressional district lines, so a few towns in a county use a different office; the county card names them.

name: CHOICES and Connecticut’s Area Agencies on Aging
organization: Connecticut Department of Aging and Disability Services and the five Area Agencies on Aging
description: CHOICES is Connecticut’s statewide line for aging and long-term care questions. It is a partnership of the Department of Aging and Disability Services, the Center for Medicare Advocacy and the Area Agencies on Aging. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call CHOICES at 1-800-994-9422, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (CHOICES, Connecticut’s SHIP)
organization: Connecticut Department of Aging and Disability Services, CHOICES
description: Free Medicare counseling from CHOICES, Connecticut’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Area Agencies on Aging.
next_step: Call CHOICES at 1-800-994-9422, or the Area Agency on Aging that serves your town. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

source_evidence.title: Connecticut ADS: CHOICES brochure (2022)
source_evidence.scope: Questions about Medicare? Call CHOICES at 1-800-994-9422 or your Area Agency on Aging; search excerpt.

name: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman and elder abuse reporting
organization: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman Program; Department of Social Services, Protective Services for the Elderly
description: Free, confidential advocacy for residents of nursing homes, residential care homes and assisted living. Protective Services for the Elderly takes reports of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment of people 60 and older living in the community.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 1-866-388-1888. To report elder abuse, call Protective Services for the Elderly at 1-888-385-4225 (weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.); after hours, call 2-1-1. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

source_evidence.scope: Toll-free 1-866-388-1888; read in full.

source_evidence.title: Connecticut DSS: Report Elder Abuse

name: Free legal help for Connecticut veterans and older adults
description: Statewide Legal Services is the usual entry point for free civil legal aid in Connecticut. It gives advice by phone or refers callers to a local legal services office or private attorney at no cost.
next_step: Call Statewide Legal Services at 1-800-453-3320 (860-344-0380 from Middletown and Hartford). People 60 and older can also call 2-1-1 for the nearest elder law office.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.

source_evidence.scope: Statewide Legal Services, 1-800-453-3320 or 860-344-0380, the entry point for legal assistance; search excerpt.

source_evidence.title: Connecticut ADS: Affordable legal help
source_evidence.scope: Statewide Legal Services 800-453-3320; over 60, visit CTLawHelp or call 2-1-1; search excerpt.

name: VA health care in Connecticut
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Connecticut Healthcare System
description: Connecticut veterans are served by the VA Connecticut Healthcare System: the West Haven VA Medical Center (950 Campbell Avenue; 203-932-5711) and the Newington campus (555 Willard Avenue; 860-666-6951), with community clinics.
next_step: For appointments, call 866-808-7921. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

name: Access Independence
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Office: 300 Long Beach Boulevard, Suite 1, Stratford.

name: Community Renewal Team, Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-CT-021): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 860-778-2423.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
